surprises: Self-caught before publication: the first shard draft TYPED its numbers into the prose. An ARN-extractor bug (reading only node['id'] and missing the 1,218 nodes carrying node['arn']) changed the measured population from 1,689 to 1,350, and the typed prose would have shipped saying 1,689 beside a run that produced 1,350. The generator now interpolates every number from one measurement dict.

The face's own L1 citation @16cd74c870 is the wrong vintage for the PLANE definition -- 1.0.0_SA_CTO~X established (79881) that it landed @398f1aa677 and that the censused pin never defines PLANE. The shards cite the corrected pin.

The re-emission was triggered, RETRACTED and re-triggered inside ten minutes: the first schema v2 @e4301b85f7 carried x_provenance.rectangle_pin = a0adeafd90 (the v1 rectangle) while every copied value came from v2. 3.0.0_SA_CVO~X read the provenance block and REFUSED; the issuer's relay had read the enum and the plane_ruling and not that field. I had already regenerated my three shards against the refused pin -- NOTHING COMMITTED -- so I preserved them to scratchpad with digests and restored the shared tree to @881ce8091e, because a refused re-emission sitting in a worktree other seats' instruments read is a hazard even uncommitted. I then verified the corrected pin's provenance field MYSELF at source before acting on it, rather than on the from-line, and still held for the issuer's relay rather than self-authorising on my own agreement.

My re-measured ARN population (1,689 -> 21 services) is BELOW L1's carried floor (1,851 -> 22). I do not reconcile it by preferring either number: the motif_to_arn NUMERATORS reproduce exactly (1,492 edges, 1,101 children) while the DENOMINATOR does not, which locates the disagreement in the ARN population rather than in the bridge.
